steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with a piece of aluminum foil and lightly grease.
Peel turnips, and cut into French fry-sized sticks, about 1/3 inch by 4 inches. Place into a large bowl and toss with vegetable oil to coat.
Combine Parmesan, garlic salt, paprika, and onion powder in a resealable plastic bag; shake until well mixed.
Place turnips into the bag and shake until evenly coated with the spices.
Spread out onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until the outside is crispy and the inside is tender, about 20 minutes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Crispy Turnip “Fries”
raw_recipe.description: Delicious crispy turnip “fries” for when you want something different than potatoes or are looking for a low-carb alternative to French fries.

review.reviewBody: I ate 4 servings even though I think the recipe needs work, so I gave it 4 stars instead of 3. :) I used 1/2 cup of cheese instead of 1/3, and fresh garlic because I didn't have garlic salt, and no onion powder because I didn't have that either. All of that was fine. I also used two tbsp oil instead of one, that was a mistake, too greasy. I baked them for 20 minutes at 425 and cranked up the oven to 450 and watched them for another couple minutes - took them out when the edges on two or three started to burn. Whoever said the cheese was the only thing crispy about these... I had that experience also. #1 change these need is something to crisp them up on the outside. I didn't have to turn them, although maybe that would have helped. Cutting them thinner (more like shoestrings than pub fries) might have helped too - the thinner ones seemed a bit crisper. The flavor was good though. They're just a little sweet, which is nice. No, they don't taste just like potato fries. Soy milk doesn't taste just like dairy milk, and veggie burgers don't taste just like beef burgers. I like these things for what they are, not how much they do or don't taste like something else, but to each their own. If you're looking for potato fries, try potatoes; but if you don't mind something a little different, give these a go.

These were amazing! No, they aren't crispy like fries but they are a great alternative if you are looking for low carb or for adding more or different veggies into you meal rotation. I pretty much made exactly using my own purchases spice mix called Nick's Mix which is similar to Lawry's but spicier. I didn't wait for the oven to pre-heat, just put it all in and set the timer for 30 minutes. I took one out and tested it and it was super yummy. I let the rest sit for another 5 or 10 minutes or so. They are phenomenal!!! (p.s. first time for turnips for me, pleasantly surprised!).

I read the reviews before I proceeded with this recipe and it turned out quite well. The only significant change I made was I used rutabaga instead of turnip because that is what I had on hand. I put the cut rutabaga and oil and seasonings in a plastic container, shook to coat and let them sit in the container for an hour or so, shaking ever so often. They took a while to cook and I turned the rutabaga frequently, about every 6 or 7 minutes, to avoid burning. I also did them in the toaster oven because I did a small batch. I love rutabaga to begin with and these were a very pleasant surprise. I have since made them several times and I have made them with both turnip and rutabaga, and in my opinion, the rutabaga fries are much better.

I've recently discovered my hand cranked spiralizer. This is a perfect recipe for that. It takes longer to peel the turnip when you can spiralize it in seconds. I did peel it, though, first. I used my smallest blade to make spaghetti noodles. Big turnips are hard to do so use the smaller ones. I've also made this with jicama and sweet potatoes. You can use any combination of spices. With the jicama I used chili powder and cayenne. I place the spiralized turnip on the sheet pan, sprinkle with oil and spices and mix with my hands. This is an easy, versatile recipe.

I'm on a low carb diet & wanted to try these. I cut them pretty thin like shoestring fries and used what I had in the pantry: olive/grapeseed/canola blend oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, parm cheese, some garlic herb seasoning salt, and for kicks I tossed in some garlic/parm popcorn seasoning since I had it sitting around. The smoked paprika gave it a great flavor & aroma combined with all the garlic. I baked for 15 minutes, turned them (they were still soggy at that point), then baked for another 10 on an insulated cookie sheet. DELICIOUS! My husband & 4-yr old son loved them too! They didn't crisp up much, but very flavorful. Recommend!

I made this recipe tonight. I have a picture, looks the same only on a white plate, I have no idea how to resize it to post here, though. I used Cajun seasoning. I did not use foil or oil on the baking pan, because I used a pampered chef bar pan and it doesn`t require oiling. I put 1 Tsp. olive oil in with the seasoning and shook after adding the turnips, until evenly coated. All I can say is Yummy !

I think this recipe is great! I substitute the olive oil for coconut butter flavour oil, used Garlic powder, salt, thyme and parsley on mine. I also pre-baked the turnip for 20 minutes before putting anything on them. I cut them up small just to get a good coat of oil and spices.

I made this but did not use any cheese. I used a little Old Bay seasoning, 2 tablespoons of Corn starch with the garlic and onion powder. They crisped up nicely and are a pleasant treat. For those who don’t seem to get them crispy, try the corn starch trick and make sure you let them get completely dry before adding the oil. We will make these again!!

What a creative idea! Its kind of like doing the same thing with yucca root. I added my own twist to this. 

Instead of putting in the oven I used my Salad Master sauce pan and put a thin layer of safflower oil. I still did the bag mix only I put parmesan cheese with a hint of caribbean fish seasoning. The trick is to fry on medium low temp stove top.

I made yummy a salad with fresh spinach, red leaf lettuce, a little carrot, mushrooms, strawberries, purple cabbage shavings. 

I topped the salad with the fried turnips..yummy!

These are an absolutely delicious, low carb alternative to potato fries! I used one Rutabaga and I wrapped the cut pieces up in a flour sack towel after cutting them into 1/4"-1/2" strips for around 20-30 minutes before oiling and seasoning them. (Don't over oil them, just so the draining sticks) Spread them in a single layer over TWO baking trays! Then I cooked them for 20 mins...took them out and flipped them, then returned them to the oven for another 10 mins. (In an electric oven) They are aren't SUPER crispy, but they are about like sweet potato fries! I will most definitely do these again! My husband ate almost one whole tray before dinner was served!

I thought these were great. A few reviewers mentioned that the "fries" weren't crispy, so I added a shake or two of panko to the bag with the seasonings and cheese. I cut mine into steak fry shape, and they needed probably twice as long in the oven, but they came out with a nice crunch from the panko, and I enjoyed them very much. I will definitely make again using smoked paprika next time and perhaps a sharper cheese like romano or asiago. Thanks IM COOKIN!!
The flavor was good, but I was hoping for them to be crispy. I'll have to try it again and see if I can get a better crisp on them.
These turned out perfect. They had a great taste, too.

Used olive oil spray. Seasoning spot on. Cutting 1/4 " thick texture similar to sweet potato fries. Was just OK taste. Will continue using turnips in Soups and stews instead. Thanks for chance to try a different way though. Certainly was a simple side to make.
They taste good but they are NOT crispy at all. I cooked them an additional 20 minutes and it didn’thelp!
Different way to have turnips. Used real parmesan cheese and cayenne pepper to add some heat

I neglected to coat with oil the first time, and put on too much spice. The third time , I rotisseried the turnips at °200, and did not coat well with oil. They too were not crispy until they got burnt. I'm encouraged that, once I remember to coat with oil, THEN season, I will get those golden brown, delectable turnip fries! I even like them half crunchy already!!
Love making my homemade French fries much the same way. I like mine crunchy so I baked them longer than recipe calls for, much longer. Still not as long as potatoes and a lot more flavorful.
The taste was fine...I prefered the extra crispy fries. They are definitely not a substitute for french fries, but are a great way to eat a different vegetable!
Flavor was good, but these were squishy not crispy. I tried a few seconds under the broiler, but that didn’t help.
